title: An invoice synced again after a tier change sends the same prices
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin whose role has 'Settings — Parts', 'See Financial Data', 'Customers — View', 'Customers — Create & Edit', 'Work Orders — Order Parts' and 'Work Order Lines — Create & Edit'.
  • Use staging with the QuickBooks sandbox connected, and sign in to that QuickBooks sandbox in a second browser window.
  • Have a new category for this test, category A, priced by a new matrix for this test, matrix A, with one cost range ($0.00 and up) whose Default rule is Markup % 35.
  • Have a new tier for this test, tier A, with a name no other tier uses, whose column in matrix A is % Off 10.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A, put on tier A for work orders in Edit Customer.
  • Have a new work order for this test, work order 1, for customer A, made after customer A's tier was set, with one labor line (line 1), with a tier-priced part in category A at $121.50, invoiced and synced to QuickBooks.
  • Use a desktop browser window at least 1440 pixels wide, at 100% zoom, so every column of the page shows.
custom_steps:
1. Click the Tiers tab on Settings › Pricing.
  2. Click tier A's row on the Tiers list.
  3. Check matrix A.
  4. Type 20 in the bulk bar's value.
  5. Click Set Rule.
  6. Click Set Rule in the dialog.
  7. Open work order 1.
  8. Sync the invoice to QuickBooks again from its Finance tab.
  9. Open the invoice in the QuickBooks sandbox.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The Tiers list shows.

Step 2:

  • Tier A's page opens.

Step 3:

  • The bulk bar shows the count 1.

Step 4:

  • % Off is picked with the value 20.

Step 5:

  • The Set Rule question opens.

Step 6:

  • Matrix A's row reads 20% off.

Step 7:

  • Work order 1's part still reads $121.50.

Step 8:

  • The invoice syncs again.

Step 9:

  • The QuickBooks line still reads $121.50, not $108.00 ($135.00 × 0.80).
